claim: Visitor, one landlord/collector, selected route and imagined negotiation are illustrative, not a documented personal diary or sale.
limit: No invented price, named victim, quantity sold or exact journey duration.

claim: In Edo, human waste was collected and traded for use as agricultural fertilizer; night soil could include feces and urine and collection was not restricted to night.
limit: Not uniquely invented in Japan; no universal separation of urine/feces or night-only activity.

claim: In Edo rental nagaya, rights over shared-privy night soil could belong to landlords, who contracted with farmers and received payment.
limit: No automatic payment to every tenant, no universal landlord annual income figure, no Osaka urine-ownership rule transplanted.

claim: Farmers or agents collected night soil for money or produce, linking town waste supply and agricultural production.
limit: No claim every exchange was barter or direct; no fixed Edo rice payment from Kanazawa.

claim: Human waste has fertilizer value through nutrients including nitrogen and phosphorus; quality was discussed in historical agricultural writings.
limit: No magical status-based quality law, exact nutrient quantity or Edo laboratory analysis.

claim: Night soil was one among several manure/fertilizer sources, and collection/storage/application involved agricultural knowledge.
limit: No exact safe treatment recipe or claim storage guaranteed pathogen elimination.

claim: The material contains much water and is heavy; land transport used paired shoulder buckets, horses or small handcarts and required labour.
limit: No unaudited capacity ratios, exact load weight or universal collection frequency.

claim: River transport connected eastern villages to Edo and allowed larger loads; boats could carry goods toward town and fertilizer on return.
limit: Use schematic cargo craft, not an exact surviving later boat. Goods and waste separate legs, no cross-contamination visual.

claim: Transport assets and labour cost money; farmers unable to provide them could depend on dealers or wealthier farmers.
limit: No claim all collectors were poor outcasts or all sellers wealthy; no invented class statistics.

locator: Koshigaya1845 paragraph; Katsushika seasonal price passage
limit: Date earlier agreement explicitly; no guaranteed10percent saving or universal price curve.

claim: A May1867notice described dealers diluting cargoes with water and deceptive load accounting, and threatened punishment; an implementing agreement required records and action against fraud.
limit: Officially reported problem and prescribed response, not proof of prevalence, successful arrests or all dealers cheating.

limit: General health fact, not measured1867infection rate or claim any shown character became ill. No DIY application advice.

locator: Synthesis of market and transport evidence
limit: Not waste-free utopia, infinitely closed loop or all participants benefiting equally.
